User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user in the ParkSmart system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

registrationDate.description: Date and time the user registered.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Parking Location entity.

latitude.description: Latitude coordinate of the parking location.

longitude.description: Longitude coordinate of the parking location.

totalSlots.description: Total number of parking slots available at this location.

hourlyRate.description: Hourly rate for parking at this location.

ParkingSlot.title: ParkingSlot
ParkingSlot.description: Represents a single parking slot within a parking location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Parking Slot entity.

slotNumber.description: Identifier or number of the slot.

isAvailable.description: Indicates if the slot is currently available.

Booking.title: Booking
Booking.description: Represents a parking booking made by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Booking entity.

userName.description: Name of the person making the booking.

entryDateTime.description: Date and time the booking starts.

exitDateTime.description: Date and time the booking ends.

bookingDateTime.description: Date and time the booking was made.

status.description: Status of the booking (e.g., active, completed, cancelled).

definition.description: Stores user profile information. Secured by Firebase Authentication; only the user can read/write their own document.

params.name: userId

definition.description: Stores information about parking locations, including name, coordinates, total slots, and hourly rate. Write access restricted to authorized admins.

definition.description: Stores information about individual parking slots within a parking location. The `parkingLocationId` parameter ensures that each parking slot is associated with a specific parking location. Write access restricted to authorized admins.

params.name: parkingSlotId

definition.description: Stores booking information for each user. Secured by path-based ownership: only the user can read/write their own bookings. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who made the booking.

params.name: bookingId
params.description: The unique identifier for the booking.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support a secure and scalable parking slot booking system (ParkSmart). The structure prioritizes authorization independence through denormalization and structural segregation to simplify security rules and enhance debuggability.

**Authorization Independence (Denormalization):**
To avoid using `get()` calls in security rules, the structure denormalizes relevant authorization data. For example, the `Booking` collection, which is a subcollection of `/users/{userId}`, inherits its authorization context from the parent `user`.  This ensures that the security rules for bookings can be evaluated independently without needing to fetch parent user data.

**Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
The data is segregated into collections based on access requirements. User-specific data (bookings) are placed under `/users/{userId}` which is secured by path-based ownership. Public data like parking locations are stored in the root collection `/parking_locations`.

**Access Modeling:**
*   **User Data:** Uses path-based ownership for user-specific data like bookings (`/users/{userId}/bookings/{bookingId}`).
*   **Public Data:** Parking locations are accessible globally through the `/parking_locations` collection.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
The structure supports secure listing operations by enforcing consistent security rules across documents within each collection.  For example, listing bookings under a specific user is secure because of the path-based ownership enforced by the rules.  Listing parking locations is also secure because it's a public collection, and security rules can restrict write access to authorized users only.

**Invariants:**
The data structure supports the integrity of ownership and timestamps by storing bookings under the respective user ID, ensuring ownership is easily verifiable via path. Timestamps like `bookingDateTime` are enforced by security rules during creation.
